title: Lost phone, remote wipe decision
symptom: A company phone with work email and apps has been lost
user_description: I think I left my work phone in a taxi last night. It has all my email and the customer app on it. What should I do?

options.text: Wait a few days in case it turns up
options.why: Anyone who finds it has time to try to get in.

options.text: Keep ringing it until someone answers
options.why: Worth a try alongside the real steps, but it does nothing to protect the data.

options.text: Do nothing because the phone has a PIN
options.why: A PIN helps, but company data still needs protecting, and policy usually requires reporting a lost device.

options.text: Remote lock or wipe it through the company's device management (for example Intune), reset his password, sign him out of sessions and report it as the policy says
options.why: Device management lets IT protect company data even when the phone is gone. A password reset and sign-out stop anyone using saved sessions.

hints: Can IT control a company phone remotely?
Could someone use apps that are already signed in?
Does the company have a rule for lost devices?
real_world_tip: A remote lock can buy time if the phone might be found. Wipe once it is clearly lost, because a wiped phone can no longer be tracked.
